messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need to lock sequencing and launch checkpoints for the private deployment roadmap. Customer asks from fintech + pharma are pushing VPC control plane + on‑prem packaging + airgap, but we can’t do all at once. Proposing a 3-phase path. Thoughts?
Priya: +1 to phased. we should be explicit about minimum viable acceptance criteria per phase. otherwise sales will expect instant parity with hosted API.
Sam: Agreed. Phase ideas?
Alex: Phase A: VPC-hosted control plane (customer VPC, Redwood-managed control plane services). Phase B: Customer-hosted control plane option (on-prem or customer VPC with customer's infra). Phase C: Air-gapped installer/bundle for fully offline environments.
Elena: Practical note: telemetry & logs are the biggest blocker for airgap customers. We need an offline telemetry strategy (local log sink + periodic export via USB/S3) and clear opt-in.
Marco: Also KMS/HSM integration is non-negotiable for pharma. Need supported patterns in Phase A (KMS in customer account) and expanded in Phase B/C for HSM appliances.
Priya: Can we sketch acceptance criteria for Phase A so PM/Eng/Sales are aligned? Proposed: 
- Control plane deployed in customer VPC with single-tenant endpoint
- Auth via customer OIDC + per-route RBAC
- Metrics & traces forwarded to customer-managed observability (CloudWatch/Datadog)
- KMS integration (customer CMK) for service secrets
- Failover plan: region fallback to Redwood-hosted for emergencies (opt-in)
Is that close?
Sam: That’s good. Add: SLA target: 99.9% for control plane management path, and clear SLO for model inference still enforced via Dedicated nodes.
Elena: For telemetry forwarding we should support a push model to customer endpoints and a pull model for on-prem. We must document what we store locally and retention defaults.
Alex: Good. For Phase B acceptance criteria (customer-hosted control plane): 
- Installer for control plane services (k8s helm chart + CRDs)
- Minimal external dependencies (no outbound except for license activation)
- Migration tooling from Phase A to Phase B (state export/import)
- Upgrade path: in-place rolling upgrades + canary channel
Marco: Question: for on-prem we’ll need an automated health-checker and an offline devkit for SRE teams. Also, legal requires exportable audit logs in immutable format.
Priya: Can we put rough timelines into quarters? Sales needs Q target to tell customers. My suggestion: 
- Q3: Phase A pilot with 2 customers (fintech sandbox, healthcare partner)
- Q4: Phase A GA + docs + enterprise onboarding runbook
- Q1 next year: Phase B alpha with 1 customer, expand KMS/HSM patterns
- Q2 next year: Phase C airgap pilot
Thoughts?
Alex: That pacing feels realistic. Risks: packaging complexity, test coverage for upgrades, and legal review timelines. We should tie these to OKRs.
Sam: From eng side, major work items: control plane networking templates, RBAC & auth integration, per-tenant KMS wiring, deployment test harness, and rollout automation. Each is ~3–6 weeks depending on parallelization.
Elena: Add: test matrix for airgap: zero-outbound, limited-proxy, and full-offline. Need automation for verifying no DNS/HTTP egress.
Marco: Regarding airgap bundles: we should support two formats: "container-bundle + installer script" for customers with container runtime, and "VM appliance" for brownfield sites. That affects packaging team scope.
Priya: Sales asks: pricing model for private — reserved capacity vs. subscription for control plane + per-node inference cost for on-prem. We should coordinate finance and legal early.
Alex: Agreed — I’ll sync with finance. Also want to propose minimal launch checklist items for Phase A GA: 
- Docs: deployment guide + troubleshooting + security FAQ
- 2 pilots signoff (SRE + customer success)
- E2E test harness passing on customer VPC templates
- KMS test matrix completed
- Rollout playbook + rollback procedure
- Legal/compliance signoff (data handling + export controls)
Can someone volunteer to own this checklist for Phase A?
Priya: I can co-own with customer success for pilot readiness.
Sam: I’ll take the E2E test harness and rollout automation.
Elena: I’ll own telemetry & logging acceptance and the airgap test matrix.
Marco: I’ll scope packaging formats and HSM integrations.
Alex: Great. One more technical note — we should standardize a small control plane config so customers can validate quickly. Example: 
```
control_plane:
  mode: vpc
  endpoints:
    api: https://cp.customer.example.com
  auth:
    oidc_provider: https://accounts.customer.example.com
  kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-1234
```
Keep this in the public doc as a starting template.
Priya: Can we draft a short FAQ for sales on differences between Phase A/B/C so they can set expectations? I’ll start one after this thread.
Alex: Perfect. Follow-ups: Sam to drop a JIRA epic list by EOD, Marco to list packaging implications, Elena to enumerate telemetry options. I’ll package this into a roadmap PR for the Product OKRs.
DevOpsBot: New ticket created: INFRA-4921 "Private deploy: Phase A GA checklist" assigned to Priya, Sam, Elena, Marco.
Priya: Thanks — I'll update pilot plan and share with CS.
Sam: Will post a rough Gantt for eng tasks tomorrow.
Alex: Thanks all. If anyone has customer-specific constraints we missed (regulatory domains, country-level data residency), drop them here or ping me directly.
